q: A stray dog presents with a compound femoral fracture and severe internal hemorrhage, wearing a collar with a rabies tag and a legible microchip. The legal stray hold is 5 days. What is the correct protocol?
o: Euthanize immediately without documentation to save costs
Provide palliative stabilization, attempt to contact the owner, and perform immediate humane euthanasia only if a licensed vet documents irremediable suffering in writing and with photos
Wait out the 5-day hold with no analgesia to preserve bloodwork
Move the dog to the adoption floor for 2 hours to see if a rescue claims it
e: A vet must document irremediable suffering in writing (photos advisable) to euthanize before the hold; ID triggers owner tracking and interim palliative care.

q: Why do manufacturers add phenytoin to sodium pentobarbital in some euthanasia formulations?
o: It acts as a local anesthetic to prevent stinging during SC injection
It causes skeletal muscle paralysis before loss of consciousness
It speeds cardiac arrest and, as a combination product, is DEA Schedule III rather than Schedule II, increasing shelter accessibility
It neutralizes the drug's toxicity on human skin contact
e: Phenytoin is a cardiotoxic adjunct; the combination product is Schedule III (vs Schedule II for pentobarbital alone), which improves shelter access.

q: Giving IV sodium pentobarbital to a calm adult dog, what is the operational sequence of stages?
o: Medullary paralysis, involuntary excitement, surgical anesthesia, voluntary excitement
Sedation, involuntary excitement, light anesthesia, deep anesthesia, apnea then cardiac arrest
Apnea, surgical anesthesia, involuntary excitement, deep sedation
Voluntary excitement, medullary paralysis, light anesthesia, deep sedation
e: The operational IV sequence is sedation, involuntary excitement, light anesthesia, deep anesthesia, then apnea followed by cardiac arrest.

q: A technician euthanizing feral kittens by IP pentobarbital makes which critical error?
o: Dosing at 3 mL per 10 lb (4.5 kg)
Inserting the needle into the upper left quadrant to target the spleen
Aspirating before injection to confirm the needle is not in bladder or bowel
Placing kittens in a dark, quiet space after injection
e: IP injection must go into the right lower quadrant to avoid liver, spleen, and kidney; aiming at the spleen is the error.

q: Which constellation is specifically diagnostic of compassion fatigue (secondary traumatic stress)?
o: Boredom with tasks, feeling underpaid, and a clean facility
Feeling powerless, intrusive thoughts, guilt, paranoia, sleep disturbance, plus stomach ulcers and high blood pressure
A desire for professional development and extra shifts
Switching from humor to more regular exercise
e: Compassion fatigue presents with powerlessness, guilt, intrusive thoughts, paranoia, sleep disturbance, and physical signs like ulcers and high BP.

q: A premix of acepromazine and ketamine is used to sedate an aggressive dog. What is a key limitation of acepromazine?
o: It provides profound analgesia and fully protects the handler
It can cause paradoxical CNS stimulation or aggression and lowers blood pressure, making venipuncture difficult
It converts the compound from Schedule III to Schedule I
It is a neuromuscular blocker causing paralysis while conscious
e: Acepromazine gives no analgesia and no protection from aggression, can cause paradoxical stimulation, and lowers BP, complicating venipuncture.

q: A near-term pregnant dog undergoes a population-control ovariohysterectomy. What is the most humane fetal handling?
o: Cut the uterus open immediately to expose fetuses to air and light
Remove the uterus en bloc, keep it intact and unopened, and wrap it so the fetuses pass away undisturbed via hypoxia in a closed system
Perform chest compressions on each fetus through the abdominal wall
Submerge the intact uterus in a chilled water bath
e: Keeping the uterus intact and wrapped lets fetuses pass undisturbed; opening it can transition a near-term fetus to air-breathing and a struggle to breathe.

q: Which pair of tools is used to definitively confirm death in a dog or cat before disposal?
o: Microchip scanner and calculator
Stethoscope (cardiac arrest) and penlight (loss of corneal reflex)
Pulse oximeter and leather gloves
Thermometer and blood pressure cuff
e: Confirm death with cardiac auscultation by stethoscope and loss of the corneal reflex checked with a penlight, regardless of method.

q: Regarding snake euthanasia, which statement is correct?
o: Place the snake in a freezer overnight
The heart is about one-third of the distance from head to tail and can be located by palpation or Doppler for IC injection once anesthesia is verified
Pentobarbital can be given SC along the dorsal midline
The body can be disposed of immediately after injection
e: Freezing is unacceptable; the snake heart sits about one-third from the head, and IC is used only after verified anesthesia, with a 24 to 48 h observation hold.

q: Which layout is recommended for a dedicated euthanasia room?
o: A large room in a high-traffic hallway with upbeat music
A quiet, well-lit, well-ventilated room away from foot traffic, with a lockable door, counter-height surfaces, and access to body storage
A dark, unventilated closet next to the dog runs
A communal room where up to three animals are euthanized in view of each other
e: The euthanasia room should be quiet, well-lit, well-ventilated, low-traffic, lockable, with paperwork and procedure surfaces and morgue access.

q: Which protocol aligns with standard equine euthanasia?
o: One person using oral pentobarbital in grain
Two experienced handlers, a pre-euth tranquilizer (eg xylazine or detomidine), then IV jugular pentobarbital at 1 mL per 10 lb (4.5 kg) (often 60 to 120 mL)
Intrahepatic T61 with no sedation
Rapid cervical dislocation with heavy restraint
e: Equine euthanasia uses two experienced handlers, pre-euth tranquilizer, and IV jugular pentobarbital at 1 mL per 10 lb (4.5 kg).

q: Why is intrahepatic injection of pentobarbital classified as unacceptable?
o: The liver has no blood vessels, so absorption is impossible
The liver capsule has stretch receptors that are exquisitely painful when stimulated
It instantly denatures pentobarbital into a non-lethal compound
It requires at least 50 mL of solution
e: The liver capsule's stretch receptors make intrahepatic injection exquisitely painful, so the route is unacceptable.

q: How does the commercial label dose of pentobarbital compare to the true lethal dose?
o: Exactly equal to the lethal dose
10% lower to preserve stock
30 to 50% higher than the lethal dose, as a safety cushion for a humane death
Five times lower, so technicians must triple the directions
e: The label dose runs 30 to 50% above the lethal dose as a cushion to guarantee a humane death when given correctly.

q: A euthanasia-team member shows belligerence, chronic absenteeism, and callous animal handling. How are these categorized?
o: Mature defenses to encourage
Negative coping mechanisms or immature defenses from euthanasia-related stress
Operational efficiencies indicating good boundaries
Burnout fully resolved by quieter clippers
e: Belligerence, absenteeism, and callous handling are negative or immature defenses arising from euthanasia-related stress.

q: Which is a positive, mature coping strategy for euthanasia staff?
o: Displacing frustration onto the surrendering public
Mature defenses such as altruism, sublimation, anticipation, and humor
Withdrawing from peers and denying distress
Increasing length-of-stay metrics
e: Altruism, sublimation, anticipation, and humor are the mature defenses; the others are negative coping or unrelated.

q: A facility must euthanize fish and amphibians. Which agent and protocol is correct per the AVMA 2020 edition?
o: Oral pentobarbital paste
MS-222 (tricaine methanesulfonate) by immersion, maintained at least 30 minutes after opercular movement ceases, followed by an adjunctive method to confirm death
Carbon monoxide via a sealed aquatic chamber
Acepromazine poured into the holding tank
e: MS-222 is the only FDA-approved fish agent; AVMA 2020 raised immersion to at least 30 min after opercular movement stops, plus an adjunctive confirmatory method.

q: Why is the absence of written euthanasia criteria an operational and emotional hazard?
o: It raises municipal licensing fees
It burdens staff, lets bias and inconsistency drive decisions, and makes choices look arbitrary to stakeholders
It invalidates the DEA license automatically
It prevents using the IV route
e: Without written criteria, decisions become inconsistent and biased, burden staff, and appear arbitrary to stakeholders.

q: Which statement reflects the national landscape of shelter euthanasia regulation?
o: Every state requires a vet to press the plunger
Regulations vary; some states allow certified technicians direct access to pentobarbital, others require indirect access or veterinary oversight
Pentobarbital is unregulated in municipal facilities
All states ban pre-euth sedatives
e: State rules vary widely on technician access and veterinary oversight of pentobarbital.

q: Why does the ASV deem CO gas chambers unacceptable for shelter euthanasia?
o: It cannot be made from commercial cylinders
It poses severe human safety hazards, can explode and leak, and causes inconsistent, prolonged distress, especially in young, old, sick, or pregnant animals
It turns the coat bright red, blocking skin testing
It reacts with pentobarbital to corrode kennels
e: CO is unacceptable on humane, operational, and safety grounds: operator hazard, explosion and leak risk, and prolonged distress in vulnerable animals.

q: A feral queen and her four 3-week-old kittens are presented for euthanasia. How should this unit be processed?
o: Move kittens away and euthanize them 24 hours apart
Euthanize the mother first so she is not distressed by separation or seeing dead offspring, then the neonates immediately after
Euthanize the kittens first while restraining the mother nearby
Place them in a group room with unfamiliar adult cats first
e: The pediatric exception: euthanize the mother first, then the neonates immediately after.

q: After euthanizing a dog with sarcoptic mange, what sanitation step is required before the next animal?
o: Wipe with a dry paper towel to remove fur
Thoroughly clean all blood, urine, feces, and residue with a neutral deodorizing solution to remove alarm pheromones
Leave the table uncleaned for two hours to air-dry
Cover the residue with newspaper
e: Clean all residue with a neutral deodorizing solution to remove alarm pheromones before the next animal.

q: What is the mechanism by which CO induces hypoxia and death?
o: It is a neuromuscular blocker freezing the intercostals while the animal stays alert
It binds hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin, blocking red cells from taking up and transporting oxygen
It causes medullary paralysis within 2 to 3 seconds of skin contact
It drops gastrointestinal pH and stimulates liver stretch receptors
e: CO forms carboxyhemoglobin, blocking oxygen uptake and transport, producing hypoxia.

q: A painful dog is sedated with xylazine. What side effect can lower the quality of the euthanasia if the animal is not fasted or combined with other drugs?
o: It frequently causes vomiting in dogs and cats and lowers blood pressure, making venipuncture difficult
It permanently expands the liver capsule
It completely blocks pentobarbital at the brain
It converts the barbiturate into a Schedule I hallucinogen
e: Xylazine often causes vomiting and lowers BP (harder venipuncture, delayed pentobarbital); fast the animal or combine with ACE or ketamine.

q: How should a technician manage body language and voice with a fearful dog?
o: Shout commands and lean over the dog's head
Remain calm, quiet, and composed, work slowly, and avoid leaning over the dog, which is a threatening posture
Move fast without speaking, using maximum control-pole pressure
Let the public and media in to create a distracting crowd
e: Stay calm and slow and avoid leaning over the dog, which is intimidating and heightens fear.

q: Which scheduling strategy mitigates burnout and compassion fatigue on the euthanasia team?
o: Assign one technician to all euthanasia permanently
Rotate duties among trained staff and let technicians choose trusted coworkers or decline animals they are attached to
Restrict euthanasia to the final 10 minutes of a 12-hour shift, alone
Eliminate regular training
e: Rotate duties, allow trusted teammates, and let staff opt out of animals they are attached to.

q: Physical avian methods (thoracic compression, decapitation, cervical dislocation) are conditionally acceptable. Why does the guide advise against them?
o: They need gas chambers banned in 50 states
More humane methods exist and several experts consider these physical methods inhumane
They cause chemical explosions endangering staff
They prevent verifying death via corneal reflexes
e: They are discouraged because more humane methods are available and some experts consider them inhumane.

q: What is the primary site of action of IV pentobarbital, and how long to cross into it?
o: The liver capsule; 15 to 30 minutes
The brain; 45 to 90 seconds
The renal cortex; 5 to 15 minutes
The myocardium; exactly 4 minutes
e: Pentobarbital acts primarily on the brain, crossing in about 45 to 90 seconds after IV injection.

q: Why is the IP route favored in shelters for a 4-pound stray kitten?
o: It bypasses the brain and stops the heart in 2 seconds
It gives a humane, smooth death for fearful, feral, or small animals under 10 lb (4.5 kg) when IV access is impractical and chemical restraint is limited
It needs only 10% of the IV dose volume
It triggers voluntary excitement that clears the room of virus
e: IP is humane for small (<10 lb (4.5 kg)), feral, or fearful animals when IV is impractical and sedation options are limited.

q: In progressive shelter legislation and organizational mandates, what does EBI stand for?
o: External Body Inspection
Euthanasia By Injection
Emergency Barbiturate Intake
Environmental Biosecurity Isolation
e: EBI is euthanasia by injection, the preferred shelter method; AHA, HSUS, and NACA offer EBI training.

q: To avoid euthanizing the wrong animal, what verification sequence is required before injecting?
o: Double-check ID against paperwork, verify authorization, search the database and photos for recent reclaim calls, and re-scan for a microchip
Ask a volunteer in the hallway if they recognize the animal
Check only the cage card, assuming it is accurate
Proceed if the coat color matches a breed description
e: Confirm ID against paperwork, verify authorization, check for reclaim calls, and re-scan the microchip before any injection.

q: If CO is used despite ASV opposition, the AVMA contingencies require which gas concentration target?
o: A uniform concentration of at least 6% after animals are placed in the chamber
A maximum of 2% to keep animals calm
Exactly 12% to ensure an explosion-free margin
Any concentration as long as the chamber is indoors
e: The AVMA contingency is a flow rate adequate to rapidly reach a uniform concentration of at least 6% after loading; death still takes 10 to 20 minutes.

q: Which animals are most likely to have delayed CO uptake, prolonging time to death?
o: Only large adult dogs
Animals under 16 weeks, geriatric, sick, injured, or pregnant
Only animals over 10 years
None; CO acts uniformly across all animals
e: Animals under 16 weeks, geriatric, sick, injured, or pregnant have delayed CO uptake; CO is also explosive above 10%.

q: How does depopulation differ from euthanasia in the shelter context?
o: They are identical terms
Depopulation is the rapid destruction of a whole population in extraordinary emergencies and is a last resort, not a routine outbreak response; EBI per AVMA 2020 is preferred when feasible
Depopulation only applies to healthy animals
Euthanasia is for populations and depopulation is for individuals
e: Depopulation is population-scale and emergency-driven, a last resort; in shelters EBI per AVMA 2020 is preferred over depopulation methods when feasible.

q: Under what condition may an intracardiac injection be performed?
o: On any conscious animal if performed quickly
Only on a heavily sedated, anesthetized, unconscious, or comatose animal
On conscious cats but not dogs
Only when IV access has failed twice
e: Per ASV, IC injection may be performed only on anesthetized or unconscious animals; on a conscious animal it is unacceptable.

q: What does the ASV say about staffing for administering injectable euthanasia?
o: A single person should always work alone for consistency
Administration may require two trained people for safe and humane handling
Only a licensed veterinarian may be present
No training is needed if pentobarbital is pre-measured
e: The ASV notes that injectable euthanasia may require two trained people for safe and humane handling.
